Subject: Kickoff: Healthlytics POC access items and org bootstrap

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for agreeing to run a short POC with Healthlytics. We're excited to evaluate Redwood's inference latency and integration model. To get our environment live this week we need to capture a short list of items so we can loop internal network and security. Can you confirm the following from your side and share any templates you prefer?

- Org setup: do you provision a Redwood org + team for us, or will we create an org and invite Redwood service accounts?
- API keys: expected lifecycle, minimum scopes, and recommended safe storage guidance (we'll put production keys into our vault later).
- IP allowlist: please provide the egress/ingress CIDR ranges we need to allow and any FQDNs to whitelist for control plane calls.
- VPC peering: high-level lead time and required contact for peering config (we use AWS, account 987654321).

Attached is our POC access spreadsheet with placeholders. Our network team needs a target window for peering — ideal is Wed or Thu this week.

Can you share the MAP-style checklist and a proposed timeline so we can align?

Thanks,
Sam Torres
Head of Platform Integrations
Healthlytics

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Kickoff: Healthlytics POC access items and org bootstrap

Hi Sam — great to kick this off. Short answers up front, then a proposed MAP and timeline below.

Org setup: We typically create a dedicated Redwood org for POCs and invite two customer admins. That keeps billing/usage scoped and lets you pin model versions. We'll create the org and send invites once you provide the admin emails.

API keys: We can issue scoped API keys for the POC that expire after 30 days. For the POC we recommend one key per environment (staging/test). Keys have model-read and generate scopes. We will share a CSV template for secure key handover.

IP allowlist & FQDNs: Our control plane endpoints to permit are api.redwood.ai and s3.redwood.ai (for optional artifacts). For peered data plane traffic we'll provide a list of egress IPs — please confirm which direction (ingress/egress) your NW team prefers.

VPC peering: We can accept peering requests from AWS accounts. Typical lead time is 24–48 hours once both sides approve. Please share your VPC ID and the AWS contact; Aditya will be the technical owner here.

Proposed MAP (high-level):
- Tue (May 11): Exchange admin emails + finalize POC org name.
- Wed (May 12): Provide IP blocks & request VPC peering.
- Thu (May 13): Redwood approves peering + we provision scoped API keys.
- Fri (May 14): Smoke test inference with a 100-request load and confirm metrics.

I've attached our connection template for IPs and API key handover. Monica will coordinate contract/PR items if procurement needs visibility.

Next steps: Please fill the spreadsheet and reply with admin emails + VPC ID. If Wed/Thu peering window is tight, propose alternatives.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai

Hi team — technical note from the infra side.

1) VPC peering steps (high level):
   - Healthlytics opens a peering connection from vpc-0a1b2c3d4e5f67890 to our peer VPC (we'll create and share the peer ID).
   - Provide the VPC CIDR and route table IDs you want to advertise.
   - Once Healthlytics creates the request, our infra will accept and add the routes; we typically need the customer's route table entries to allow return traffic.

2) IP allowlist / NAT:
   - For the initial POC we can accept the two CIDRs Claire provided. We'll also provide a short list of egress IPs for callbacks (control plane). Expect that in a separate email from ops.

3) Org and API provisioning:
   - Rachel/team will create the org. For API key creation we'll ask for the username that should be listed as owner. Keys are delivered via encrypted CSV; for now treat them as temporary.

4) Minimum roles for service accounts:
   - read:models, create:inference, s3:put-object (if you plan to upload artifacts)

I'll start the peering side once Rachel confirms the target org name and we have the VPC request from Claire.

Thanks,
Aditya
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
